meeting.eyebrow: What is never written in a listing
meeting.p1: What we rarely talk about is what happens around it. Getting to know a grandmother and her story because you helped her pick her garden fruit. Exchanging with Gerardo while he gives you a small favour with DIY, and offering him a home-made meal in return.
meeting.p2: You don't need a pet for a meeting to begin. Asking for a small favour, offering one: it's already opening a door. Sitting a house is opening another, same gesture, two scales.
meeting.p3: We learn, we discover, we grow attached, without looking for it. Just by leaving space for what can happen.

how.title: How does it work?
how.step1_text: Your dates, your pets, your house. A few minutes are enough, your listing is online.
how.step2_text: Caretaker / pet & home sitters apply. You read profiles, reviews, you chat. Then you meet, a coffee, a visit, before deciding.
how.step3_text: Once the sitting agreement is signed, your sitter moves in. You receive news. You return home, often with a new relationship.
how.cta_secondary: Or start with a small favour →

aid.title: Dare to ask. Dare to propose.
aid.p1: Before, there was someone who would come by to water the garden, who looked after the dog, who came to fix a shutter. Someone to whom we offered a piece of cake or a small favour in return.
aid.p2: This habit hasn't disappeared, we simply no longer dare to ask the first question. Guardiens is the pretext to ask it again, and along the way, live experiences that no organised trip could offer you.
aid.need_text: Your vegetable garden during holidays. Your chickens this weekend. Walking your dog after an operation. Asking for it isn't admitting a weakness, it's trusting.
aid.need_footer: A service in return for a service. That's the bet.
aid.offer_title: « I can give a little of my time »
aid.offer_text: You know how to prune roses. You love dogs. You have two hours on Saturday morning. Propose, and live what you would never have experienced without this meeting.
aid.offer_footer: That is how a fabric reweaves itself.
aid.seen_this_week: A few exchanges seen on Guardiens this week
aid.quote: « Village life hasn't disappeared. It was simply waiting for someone to dare the first question. »

trust.title: Choose with confidence, one mile away or a thousand.
trust.lede: Four benchmarks for peace of mind: a meeting before every sit, documented profiles, cross reviews, and a perimeter you set yourself.
trust.p1_text: Between members, everything happens without a transaction: a service in return for a service.
trust.p2_text: A coffee, a visit of the accommodation, a tour of the instructions. Trust isn't guessed: it is built, face to face.
trust.p3_text: Every profile displays reviews published by previous owners and the history of completed sits. An in-person meeting before every sit remains at the heart of trust.
trust.p4_title: From your street to the other side of France
trust.p4_text: Close to home for a quick fix, across the country for a change of scenery: you decide how far you want to go. Every sit becomes an opening door.

testimonials.title: They dared. Here is what they kept.
testimonials.source: Testimonials collected from our early members (January to May 2026). Real first names and cities, stories anonymised at their request.

items.nadia: Two cats and a dog. We had not taken a real holiday in three years. Our sitter lives ten minutes away. We met over a coffee on the Thursday. We left on the Saturday.
items.tomas: I was looking for a place to stay between two jobs. I sat four houses in two months. I discovered places I had lived next to for ten years without ever really knowing them.
items.rania_david: We have a house in Ardèche that sat empty eight months a year. Now it is alive. The people who look after it send us photos of the garden. It is strange how good that feels.
items.giulia: I had to leave for three weeks. My vegetable patch, my hens, my plants. A Guardiens member handled it all in exchange for vegetables and eggs. We did not know each other. We still see each other.
items.sarah_karim: Three horses, four cats, a parrot. Everyone tells us that is impossible to have looked after. Our sitter came twice before we left. She knew their names by heart.
items.elena: I started by watering a member's plants in exchange for a meal. Now I look after her house when she travels. That is how it works here, slowly, naturally.

story.title: It all started with a visa.
story.p1: The habit of opening up to others has been lost. For lack of a pretext.
story.p2: Elisa, my partner and co-founder of Guardiens, arrived from Argentina with a visa that didn't allow her to work. She looked after pets. She would come home with stories: people opening their doors, their lives, freely. Strangers who ended up inviting us for Christmas.
story.p3: Elisa and I looked after 37 houses in five years, in villages, cities, and hamlets.
story.quote: We never looked after houses. We were invited into lives.
story.p4: That's what the village used to do naturally.
story.p5: Guardiens is the pretext that was missing. On one side, small favours of mutual aid between members: a vegetable garden watered in exchange for a meal, one skill for another, a small favour returned in kind. On the other, independently, house-sitting: your keys entrusted to someone you've looked in the eye.
story.p6: You will leave with peace of mind. You will return with a story. We didn't expect it to matter so much.
story.p7: That's why we built Guardiens, so you could live this too.
story.quote_lead: One evening, an owner told him:
story.p8: One evening at Helen's, Stanley barking, Rafa lying on our feet, the view over Mont Blanc. We thought: why aren't more people doing this?
story.p9: That is why we built Guardiens.
story.p10: Your garden for a meal. Your keys for a story. People from the area who trust each other, and sometimes friends for life.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.a1: House-sitting is a service exchange: a caretaker / pet & home sitter lives free of charge in your house during your absence and takes care of your pets. The exchange involves no financial transaction between the two parties.
faq.q2: Do I have to pay to register as an owner?
faq.a2: Registration, listing publication and exchanges with sitters are subscription-free for owners. No credit card required. Guardiens stays free as long as we are not satisfied with the service we offer you. You have full access, no limits, no commitment.
faq.q3: How can I find a pet sitter near me?
faq.a3: Register on Guardiens, publish your sitting listing with dates and your pets, and receive applications from caretaker / pet & home sitters who live near you. You choose after a meeting.
faq.q4: Who are the sitters on Guardiens?
faq.a4: People you can trust. Identity verification is open to every member, and validated profiles display the « Identity verified » badge. Trust is built on the in-person meeting held before every sit, on cross-reviews published after each experience, and on the history visible on every profile.
faq.q5: How does a sit take place on Guardiens?
faq.a5: You publish your listing, caretaker / pet & home sitters apply, you choose after a meeting, then your sitter moves in. An optional sitting agreement frames the commitments of each party during the sit.
faq.q6: Is Guardiens available everywhere in France?
faq.a6: Yes. The Guardiens network extends to all regions of France, from the Basque Country to Brittany, through the Alps and the North. You will find a sitter near you regardless of your department.
faq.q7: What is the Guardiens business model?
faq.a7: Guardiens stays free as long as we are not satisfied with the service we offer you. You get access to everything, with no limit and no commitment. You will be told in advance when that changes.
faq.a8: Identity verification is open to every member: the document sent in is analysed automatically, files that do not pass this first check are reviewed by our team, and validated profiles display the « Identity verified » crest. A meeting between the owner and the sitter before the stay is strongly recommended. After each experience, the cross reviews published on the profile build a verifiable reputation, visible to all members.

what_is.title: What is Guardiens?
what_is.body_1: Guardiens is a mutual aid network between individuals, organised by affinity as much as by proximity. People look after homes, do each other favours, and meet. One kilometre away, or a thousand.
what_is.body_2: House sitting and in-home pet sitting form its main use. A sitter moves into your home while you are away and looks after what you leave behind: your house, your garden, your pets.
what_is.body_3: Beyond sits, members give each other a hand: watering, shopping, company. The exchange is decided between you.
what_is.body_4: Matching relies on an affinity score calculated on seven criteria, where lifestyle counts as much as distance. Every profile is documented, identity is verified, reviews are cross-checked. An emergency sitter status answers the unexpected.
what_is.body_5: Guardiens also publishes breed guides and local guides, city by city. They are joined by a directory of animal professionals whose business number (SIRET) is checked, and a journal of practical advice.
what_is.body_6: The network covers all of France, and connects French people living abroad with sitters on site. You have access to everything, with no commitment.

emergency_page.meta_title: Emergency Pet Sitter for your animals | Guardiens
emergency_page.meta_description: Need an emergency sitter for your pets? Activate the Guardiens alert: local emergency sitters are notified as a priority.
emergency_page.soon_title: Coming soon. The emergency sitter network will activate as soon as we have enough eligible and experienced sitters.
emergency_page.soon_subtitle: Our platform is young. We take the time to designate emergency sitters on strict criteria to guarantee reliability.
emergency_page.hero_lead: Your safety net. An unexpected event, a last-minute cancellation, a sudden departure? Eligible sitters can be alerted as a priority.
emergency_page.hero_tagline: That is the strength of proximity: people already on the spot, not on the other side of the country.
emergency_page.step1_title: An owner has an urgent need
emergency_page.step1_desc: Last-minute cancellation, family emergency, work trip… life doesn't always warn you.
emergency_page.step2_desc: Automatic notification sent to available emergency sitters within a 35 km radius.
emergency_page.step3_title: The stay is organized with the sitter
emergency_page.step3_desc: Quick exchange, confirmation, off we go. Pets are in good hands.
emergency_page.stories_lead: Emergencies don't always look the way you imagine. Six situations the network is designed to handle. These scenarios are illustrative, they describe how the service is meant to work.
emergency_page.story1_text: Scheduled hospitalization moved up at the last minute. Two cats at home, no one around. She activated the alert Tuesday evening. An emergency sitter, already rated by other members, replied within two hours. Meeting the next morning before departure. On return, cats still there, fridge too.
emergency_page.story2_text: Five-year-old Australian Shepherd, magnificent but reactive with strangers. Pierre had to leave for five days on a work trip. No question of a kennel. He activated the alert. An emergency sitter trained for strong-tempered dogs replied the same evening. First meeting outside, neutral ground. Pierre left reassured.
emergency_page.story3_text: Sudden death of a relative in the Paris region. Camille had to leave for four days, her 14-year-old cat can no longer handle moving. Alert sent in the morning, an emergency sitter replied before noon. The cat didn't budge. Neither did Camille, in a way.
emergency_page.story4_text: Diabetic dog, two daily injections at fixed times. No one in her circle knew how. Sophie had to be away three days. She activated the alert specifying the care skill. An emergency sitter with vet experience replied that day. Injection demo the morning of departure. Everything went as planned.
emergency_page.story5_text: Unexpected consulting mission abroad, departure in 36 hours. Two cats at home, no family in town. Thomas activated the alert Thursday evening. Friday morning, an emergency sitter came to meet the cats and get the keys. Six days away, zero stress on the cats' side.
emergency_page.story6_text: Rushed move, the previous owner brought the walk-through forward by a week. Two stressed cats, an apartment under works, no time. The alert went out at 9am, an emergency sitter replied at 11am. The cats finished the week peacefully at the sitter's place.

emergency_page.engagement_title: A commitment, not just a badge
emergency_page.engagement_p1: Being an emergency sitter is a commitment. If you decline an urgent request, no worries, it happens. But if you decline more than once, the status is removed and you cannot reactivate it for 6 months. Owners count on emergency sitter availability.
emergency_page.engagement_p2: Cancellations are reassessed every 6 months: only those from the last 6 months count for eligibility.
emergency_page.cities_lead: The emergency network relies on sitters across France. Here are the cities where the network is being built first.
emergency_page.further1_desc: For one-off helping hands (without urgency) between members.
emergency_page.further2_desc: Vets, parks, dog-friendly cafes and good spots near you.
emergency_page.further3_desc: The complete guide to join the Guardiens emergency sitter network.
emergency_page.faq1_q: How long to be contacted in an emergency?
emergency_page.faq1_a: On Guardiens, emergency alerts are prioritized: eligible emergency sitters in your radius are notified instantly (SMS, email, push). The system is designed so that a reply can arrive in the hours following the alert.
emergency_page.faq2_q: Does it work at night or on weekends?
emergency_page.faq2_a: Yes. Emergency alerts are active 24/7. At night and on weekends, notifications go first to sitters who indicated extended availability. Response times can be a bit longer in atypical slots, but the service remains active.
emergency_page.faq3_q: My dog is reactive or anxious, is it still possible?
emergency_page.faq3_a: Yes, it's even a typical emergency case. When you activate the alert, you specify your pet's profile (reactive, anxious, special care, etc.). Only emergency sitters with the required experience and skill are notified. No sitter takes a stay without meeting the pet first, that's the rule.
emergency_page.faq4_q: How much does an emergency stay cost?
emergency_page.faq4_a: For owners, signing up and using Guardiens (including the emergency alert) are free. No surcharge applies for an emergency stay compared to a classic one. The house-sitting logic remains: no money flows between you and the sitter.
emergency_page.faq5_q: What's the difference with a classic stay?
emergency_page.faq5_a: A classic stay is prepared in advance: you post your listing, get several applications, choose. An emergency stay takes a shorter path: an eligible sitter (5 stays minimum, rating 4.7+, 0 cancellations, verified identity) is notified as a priority, you meet them, then the stay can start as soon as you both agree.
emergency_page.faq6_q: What if I'm hospitalized, how does it work?
emergency_page.faq6_a: It's one of the most frequent cases. You (or a relative) activate the alert directly from your dashboard or by phone. If you cannot, a relative can do it for you with your consent. The emergency sitter takes over: house, pets, mail if needed. You take everything back on your return.
emergency_page.faq7_q: How do I become an emergency sitter on Guardiens?
emergency_page.faq7_a: Four conditions: have completed at least 5 stays on Guardiens, have an average rating above 4.7/5, no cancellations, and have a verified identity. Once these criteria are met, you can activate the status from your dashboard.
emergency_page.faq8_q: What exactly do I commit to as an emergency sitter?
emergency_page.faq8_a: To respond quickly to the alerts you receive (push, SMS, email). You are not obliged to accept each request: you can decline if you're unavailable. But you commit to responding, not ignoring.
emergency_page.faq9_q: What happens if I decline an emergency request?
emergency_page.faq9_a: The first decline has no consequence, it's normal not to always be available. However, a second consecutive decline causes loss of status for 6 months. It's our guarantee to owners: an emergency sitter is truly available.
emergency_page.faq10_q: What do I gain by being an emergency sitter?
emergency_page.faq10_a: Priority visibility in search results, early access to interesting stays, distinctive badge on your profile, and one month of subscription offered per emergency intervention. Above all: you provide a real service to members who truly need it.
emergency_page.faq11_q: How am I notified of an emergency?
emergency_page.faq11_a: SMS + email + push notification (if enabled). You configure your preferences from the dashboard: intervention radius (5 to 200 km), availability time slots, accepted pet types. Only alerts matching your preferences reach you.
emergency_page.faq12_q: Can I lose my emergency sitter status?
emergency_page.faq12_a: Yes, in several cases: rating drops below 4.7 (status paused, recoverable), cancellation of an accepted stay (immediate loss, reactivable after 5 new incident-free stays), second consecutive emergency decline (6-month suspension), expired subscription (status paused).
